trust_decision.summary: The request-authorization decision for public resources is made by the group-level read RBAC middlewares: when the user is denied but the org/project/asset is public and the action is ActionRead, the middleware sets the publicRequest context flag and calls next() instead of returning 404, so every non-GET route beneath that group must add its own write check (write-action asset RBAC or the new DisallowPublicRequests).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names no route, so an engineer looks for a destructive write on a public asset: the artifact group's DELETE and PUT carry only NeededScope and sit under the asset group whose only RBAC is assetScopedRBAC(ObjectAsset, ActionRead) (router/asset_router.go:49), which is exactly the public-read continuation.

fix_sites.entry_point: middlewares.DisallowPublicRequests (new middleware used by the routes below)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: middlewares/access_control_middlewares.go:98-143 (AssetAccessControlFactory; the same public-read continuation also lives at :67-68, :183-185 and :243-245)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: AssetAccessControlFactory is the deliberate public-read gate that an existing test pins ('allows read access to public asset'), so a solver can argue it is out of scope for a write-authorization fix and must keep letting non-members through on public assets; the real gap is that the factory cannot see the HTTP verb, which is why the published fix had to patch every route individually instead.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate behaviours sit next to the sink: anonymous read of a public asset's SBOM/VEX/triage data must keep working (the README advertises such a public instance, and a pinned test asserts the public-read continuation), and a read-only member must still be allowed to triage findings (the published fix deliberately uses DisallowPublicRequests, not an ActionUpdate RBAC, on the vuln/first-party/license-rule routes). Applying either middleware at the asset or asset-version group level breaks the first; using ActionUpdate RBAC on triage routes breaks the second.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: middlewares/access_control_middlewares.go:131-133 with middlewares/access_control_test.go:374 and README.md:105-114; member-triage carve-out stated at fix.diff:267-268

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new sub-router group under /refs/:assetVersionSlug (like the vex-rule/external-reference groups) whose POST/PUT routes carry only NeededScope([]string{"manage"})
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every existing asset-version sub-router that the fix had to patch was written exactly this way (vex rules, license risks, external references), so a maintainer adding one more feature group would copy that shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a POST route added to the crowdsourced-vexing group (e.g. accepting a recommended VEX assessment) guarded only by NeededScope
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the one asset-version sub-router that is read-only today; adding the natural accepting action would follow the sibling routers that all used NeededScope only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another fast-access asset route (scan/vex/sarif/attestation style) registered on the session group with NeededScope("scan") and no assetScopedRBAC write check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These routes are outside /api/v1/organizations and outside the fixed test's filter, and the inline comment at session_router.go:71-74 exists because maintainers already worry about forgetting the RBAC there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another write verb on the artifact subgroup (for example a POST that re-uploads or re-attaches artifact metadata) registered without a write RBAC
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The artifact subgroup is created with only ArtifactMiddleware; the only thing that protected its two write routes was a per-route middleware, so a third write route would be born unprotected.
